thesisQuality.note: Strong AI-infrastructure demand plus expansion into power/thermal/rack capabilities supports durable demand and differentiation, but customer concentration and contract economics limit an exceptional band.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Q3 exceeded expectations and FY26 guidance rose to $35B revenue, 5.8% core margin, $12.70 core EPS and >$1.4B adjusted FCF.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: Current market snapshot shows $32.35B market cap and 19.54 forward P/E: plausible growth-adjusted upside, but not rare valuation asymmetry.

catalystScore.note: September 30 FY2026 results are a dated near-term verification event following raised guidance; Adani and capability expansion add medium-term catalysts with execution uncertainty.

governancePower.note: Management has repeatedly raised outlook while emphasizing profitable growth, capital efficiency and shareholder value; acquisition/alliance execution remains to be proven.

alignment2036.note: Power, thermal, networking, rack manufacturing and integration are durable physical requirements of dense AI/data-center infrastructure and span multiple geographies.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: AI infrastructure growth coexists with improving Automotive and Connected Living, while manufacturing/engineering capabilities are reusable across end markets.

bottleneckControl.note: Jabil participates in constrained power, thermal and rack deployment layers, but does not demonstrate sole control or absence of alternative suppliers.

scenarioRobustness.note: Diversified end markets and architecture-agnostic manufacturing provide multiple demand paths, tempered by hyperscaler capex and large-customer sensitivity.

substitutionResilience.note: Qualification, manufacturing integration and broader power/thermal capability create switching friction, but customers can redesign, dual-source or vertically integrate.

supplyChainResilience.note: U.S. manufacturing investment and proposed India capacity improve geographic optionality, while packet risk evidence still identifies critical-component supplier dependence.

pricingPower.note: Raised 5.8% core operating-margin outlook and strong demand support some economic capture, but manufacturing remains competitive and direct price-pass-through evidence is limited.

risk.note: Material but non-gating risks include customer and supplier concentration, hyperscaler capex cyclicality, acquisition/alliance execution and possible customer vertical integration.

confidence.note: Identity/tradability and operating claims have current primary lineage; valuation has a current independent market source. Confidence is reduced for undisclosed customer-level AI concentration, alliance economics and pending Q4 results.

thesis: Jabil combines diversified manufacturing scale with expanding power, thermal and rack-integration capability positioned in physical AI-infrastructure constraints; current operating momentum is strong, but value capture remains exposed to customer concentration and competitive manufacturing economics.
keyRisk: A hyperscaler capex slowdown, customer redesign/vertical integration, or weak acquisition/alliance execution could compress growth and margins despite continued AI infrastructure buildout.
nextCatalyst: Fiscal Q4/FY2026 earnings and fiscal 2027 priorities scheduled for September 30, 2026.
